The discussion in this proof is a bit pedantic because we want
to carefully match the underlying categories. In this paragraph
we explain how the adventurous reader can proceed less timidly.
Namely, the reader may extend our definition of the functor <MATH_0004>
to all locally Noetherian algebraic spaces over <MATH_0005>.
Doing so the reader may then conclude that <MATH_0006> and <MATH_0007> agree as
functors on the category of these algebraic spaces, i.e.,
<MATH_0008> represents <MATH_0009>. Then one considers the universal object
<MATH_0010> in <MATH_0011>. Then the reader will find that
for the triple <MATH_0012>, <MATH_0013>, <MATH_0014> witnessing the compatibility
between <MATH_0015> and <MATH_0016> the morphism <MATH_0017> is an isomorphism
and this will produce <MATH_0018> by inverting <MATH_0019>. Finally, we already
have <MATH_0020> and the reader may show that <MATH_0021> is an isomorphism
which can served as the last ingredient namely <MATH_0022>.
